newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: RTRS-Papua New Guinea forecasts small 1997 surplus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Papua New Guinea forecasts small 1997 surplus.

text.p: The Papua New Guinea Government on Tuesday unveiled its 2.4 billion kina (US$1.8 billion) budget for calendar 1997, forecasting in parliament that it would achieve a small 7.3 million kina surplus and focus on law and order as a priority area next year.

Outlays would increase from 2.36 billion kina in 1996 and had also risen by 47.2 million kina on a preliminary 1997 forecast presented to the PNG parliament in September. Haiveta said 1997 revenue was estimated at 2.41 billion kina.

He said the budget focussed on the priority areas of health, education, transport, agriculture, law and order, and private sector development. Expenditure in these areas would rise by 25.5 percent to 697.3 million kina in 1997.
Another 21 million kina would be spent on defence and police operations on Bougainville Island where the government has been fighting a seccessionist rebellion since May 1989.
Haiveta forecast gross domestic product growth would rise to 3.8 percent next year from 3.0 percent in 1996, with inflation stable at 8.0 percent.
